done_when: the stale-identifier-on-rotate class has a gate naming F-0519, F-0520, F-0766 and F-0816, each integration's reversion turns it RED independently, and a new integration carrying the same shape is caught

evidence.command: bash .proof-os/gates/F-0519-rotate-keeps-identifier.sh plus five reversions run one at a time and restored between
evidence.result: each of the three integration reversions reds independently and names its integration; a synthetic fifth integration the gate had never seen is caught; the unmutated tree is green. The Meta reversion was reproduced independently by the dispatcher after a first attempt that mutated the wrong line and proved nothing.

not_checked: no points-to analysis proves a rotate call's argument slot could not coincidentally be some other in-scope variable; the three behavioural reconnect tests are what actually exercise the write path
the UNIQUE(shop_domain)/UNIQUE(site_url) collision case - reconnecting to an identifier a different, now-revoked workspace previously held - is pre-existing, unhandled, and declared rather than fixed
the gate does not check class-file freshness across all of com.influora; it assumes mvn -o test, never surefire:test against stale bytecode
nothing was run live: no OAuth reconnect against a real Shopify, WooCommerce or Meta account was performed, so this is proved at the persistence layer and not end to end

my own first reproduction of the Meta reversion mutated applyIgBusinessAccountId instead of the assignment inside rotateToken and was therefore meaningless; it is only the second attempt that carries any weight
